entities.label: EventWindow
entities.summary:
The Battle of Sagrajas was a pivotal event in the Reconquista, a centuries-long Christian campaign to reclaim the Iberian Peninsula from Moorish rule. Taking place on October 23, 1086, in the city of Badajoz, this battle saw the forces of King Alfonso VI of Castile clash with the Almoravid army led by Sultan Yusuf ibn Tashfin. The outcome of the battle had far-reaching consequences, shaping the trajectory of Spanish history and the fate of the Christian kingdoms in the region.

The Battle of Sagrajas was a crushing defeat for the Christian forces, with King Alfonso VI being forced to flee the battlefield. Despite this, the battle marked a turning point in the Reconquista, as the Christians regrouped and refocused their efforts. The Almoravid victory, however, came at a great cost, as the empire's military power was stretched thin by the ongoing conflict.

In the aftermath of the battle, the Almoravids continued to exert their control over the Iberian Peninsula, but their grip began to weaken. The Christian kingdoms, buoyed by the setback, continued their push southward, eventually driving the Moors from the peninsula in the late 15th century. The legacy of the Battle of Sagrajas, therefore, lies in its role as a catalyst for the eventual Christian reconquest of Spain.

The Battle of Sagrajas serves as a testament to the enduring power of faith and the indomitable will of the people, as the Christian kingdoms persevered in the face of overwhelming odds, ultimately emerging victorious in the long struggle for control of the Iberian Peninsula.
